verdict.rationale: Cursor's own docs say its agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows and verify changes. They can also control the desktop and browser and attach log artifacts, alongside a debugging workflow to 'reproduce issues, narrow the root cause, and verify the fix'. That is genuine first-party running-app interaction, but it is framed as cloud agents verifying their own changes rather than a developer debugging an already-live app. Missing for 10: attaching to an already-running/live application, debugger features (breakpoints, runtime inspection, console/network capture), in-depth docs on the debugging flow, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug a live running web application directly from my coding assistant

citations.quote: Agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows, and verify their changes work before pushing a PR.
Reproduce issues, narrow the root cause, and verify the fix
They can also use computers to control the desktop and browser
Agents create artifacts such as screenshots, videos, and log references to demonstrate their work.
